Uncharted 4: A Thief's End (+ DLC)

Good:
‣ Really good cinematics.
‣ Good story with some nice twists.
‣ Interesting characters with strong chemistry.
^ Both main characters (Base game and DLC) with their "sidekicks"
‣ Gameplay-wise, it’s simple but enjoyable: exploration, platforming, puzzles, stealth, and gunfights.
‣ The base game is fairly long, while the DLC is shorter and features a different protagonist and a different story.
‣ Base game is about pirate treasure while DLC is about an artifact tied to Hindu Mythology. (both pretty amazing settings in my opinion, tho the pirate treasure is way more expanded)
‣ unlockable outfits, filters and cheats (tho you must meet some requirements to do that)

Mixed:
‣ Enemies sometimes shoot through walls.
‣ There are a lot of scripted events.
‣ Puzzles are really simple (i don't mind it, but after playing TR Survivor trilogy, the puzzles in this game were easy to catch on).

Bad:
‣ The endgame levels and gameplay. In theory, the ideas behind the final sections of both the base game and the DLC are good, but I feel they were implemented poorly.
‣ Has no prequels/sequels on PC.

Conclusion:
‣ I don't think the game is a perfect 10/10, but i do think it's a very good one, especially if you're looking for a linear game with bits of exploration, action and platforming and a good story with interesting and memorable characters.

I only played Uncharted 4 out of this bundle.

It's not very often that I play a game where the world building is so good that it feels a bit sad when it's over. I experienced all the emotions playing this. The action set pieces were having me shout from excitement. The characters are balanced and relatable, making it easy to get invested in their story. Big game too at 20 hours and I wasn't looking for the collectables. Often I found myself saying "wow that looks great." Well optimised I was running it on max even with a GTX 1070 laptop.

If you are looking for some adventure and escapism, the whole bundle would provide hours of that. I got it as a bundle with a processor.

I'm not much of an action gamer and I had never played Uncharted before, but I gave this a shot and was blown away by the wonderful story and acting, the absolutely beautiful environments, and the exciting gameplay. I highly recommend this to anyone who may be remotely interested in an action game.

On a personal note, I have a lot of trouble with direction sense and finding my way around, even in my home city. I was therefore more than pleased to learn that this didn't require a great deal of direction sense.

Mind you, the game was often not easy and could be frustrating, but it was always fair.

First off, this is the most photogenic game I have ever played. I am not one to usually take screenshots in games, but the amount of screenshots I have taken of the scenery in this game it is just beautiful. Uncharted 4 is easily in my top 3 games, it has an amazing story with cinematic style missions. The pacing is perfect, the puzzles are not too difficult and you feel like you're in an action movie. I bought it on sale but without a doubt I would buy this for its regular price.

I've been playing tomb rider since the 90s and uncharted is new to me since its appearance on steam, both have similarities. the difference is that uncharted is an action-packed, bright and beautiful game with funny and deep dialog. if you like tomb rider but with funny dialog and a bright world, this is definitely not to be missed.

Without a doubt, this is a game with an absolutely incredible story. For the first time, I was able to enjoy an amazing game with stunning graphics and a unique adventure. After so many years of watching gameplay videos, I was finally able to experience the excitement of this title for myself.

This is a good game, one of Naughty's Dog's best achievements in graphics, shooter/stealth mechanics. If you enjoyed the trilogy, you most likely will love this game. It's a high-octane action, adventure third-person shooter with characters that resonate with each other.

Is this the same leap in quality that The Last of Us (part 1) achieved? Not really, I found this game way too long and slow at some parts, I would get back into the game and enjoy myself but the story is not that engaging IMO. I have played Uncharted 1 and 2 multiple times but I don't feel like I will return to Uncharted 4 in a very long time. Uncharted 4 takes a more grown-up approach to its story but I feel like this does not fit with the gameplay that the Uncharted series is known for. There's so much more dissonance between Drake's actions and his character compared to the earlier iterations.

Uncharted 4 certainly is not a bad game, it's a well polished game with some super fun set pieces and rich shooting mechanics. I DO recommend this game despite some of its flaws!

This game is fantastic, the only reason I know that is I've played both the games at launch multiple times over the years on PS4/PS5. However, after hours of troubleshooting and trying everything I can find to fix it, it's unplayable on PC with headphones due to the extreme audio issues. The in game audio whether you change it to 2 channel speaker, headphone, mono, etc. output, or change it from 3D spatial to traditional, or change the latency from low to high, or change Windows audio effects, sonic, etc. on and off and mess with the settings and properties, does not fix it. It's quiet, garbled, scratchy and unplayable. It seems to be a major issue with this port, and I've had the issue with 2 different PC set ups and my laptop. Changing some of the previous settings works for some people online, updating drivers or other fixes work for others. Some like me can never get it to work with headphones.

An outstandingly fun adventure with a story that has as many twists and turns as a bowl of spaghetti. Graphics are outstanding and the game runs stable at max settings on my modest rig. Every aspect of the game's design is nothing short of phenomenal. The main story lasted a bit over 13 hours. The other part of the game, The Lost Legacy, is very much worth playing as well, and is a fair bit shorter than the main game, at 5-6 hours. Given that the game relies more on its story than its gameplay, I don't think it would have very much replayability value. I don't see that as much of a negative, though. Highly recommend, especially when it goes on sale.
